newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Commission to take further drift-net soundings.
newsitem.headline: Commission to take further drift-net soundings.

text.p: The European Commission, pressed by Spain, will hold informal talks with member states on a long-standing proposal to ban drift-net fishing by the end from the end of 1997, EU officials said.

Spain and Greece were the only countries to support the European Commission's proposal of April 1994 to ban drift-nets for catching tuna, swordfish and salmon in the north-east Atlantic, Mediterranean and Baltic.
Spanish fishermen, who use the traditional hook and line method, say that they can't compete against the huge drift-nets used by French, British and Irish fishermen.

At this week's Fisheries Council, the Commission suggested one option would be to split the proposal, allowing fishermen to continue catching salmon with drift-nets in the Baltic, where fishing controls are very strict.
The Commission also said it preferred putting EU inspectors on national fishery patrol vessels due to the high cost of chartering a vessel.
The EU patrol vessel, first chartered in 1995, has helped to avoid clashes between Spanish and French fishermen in the Atlantic where the tuna drift-net fishing season is due to start in May.
Germany, noting the European Parliament's opposition to drift-nets, said it was in favour of banning this type of fishing, except in the Baltic. Italy also supported abolishing drift-nets.
But France reiterated its opposition to a drift-net ban, saying it would only force fishermen to hunt other stocks.
